summary: CCC-era 80-ft steel tower on Jack Mountain near Monterey, VA; removed 2002; restored by Skip Jones and reinstalled 2017; daylight visits reported since 2020; original site has no tower.

facts.design: 80-foot all-steel lookout tower (planned at 47 feet, changed in 1934)
facts.status_note: Dismantled and removed from the original Sounding Knob site in 2002. FFLA lists the original site as Tower Gone. The restored tower was reinstalled on Jack Mountain in 2017.

access.note: Privately owned by Skip Jones. Register says the tower is gated but was being left open for daylight visits as of November 2020; no newer confirmation found. Check with the owner.

visit.trail_note: Gravel drive off Sounding Knob Road, 1.3 miles south of Rt. 250; more than 100 steps to the top (VACo). Confirm access with the owner.

facts.agency: Virginia Department of Forestry (built); privately owned by Hammill Skip Jones since 2016

events.note: Register: built 1935 for the Virginia Department of Forestry by CCC workers. Jones and VACo say 1934; a 1934 Highland Recorder item describes the camp, road and planned tower.
Lookout watchman Jesse Wiseman moved into the tower on March 11, 1948; still on duty in October 1950.
Approximate: register says staffed until the 1960s; Jones says fire towers went out of use in the 1960s.
Disassembled and removed from its original location on Sounding Knob. Steve Good of Highland Welding bought the tower and stored its components.
A Recorder item dated July 24, 2004 reports the 80-foot tower on Sounding Knob was dismantled.
Purchased by Hammill Skip Jones. Steel and bolts re-galvanized; new hemlock steps.
Totally disassembled and restored; reinstalled on Jack Mountain with a public dedication on July 8, 2017.
Registered July 8, 2017 as US 1221, VA 39; nominated by Brian Powell.
Register says the tower and cab were being left open to visitors during daylight hours as of November 2020.

corrections.proposed: Jack Mountain, east of Monterey (same mountain; reinstalled 2017)
corrections.why: The record names the original site as the destination. FFLA lists the restored tower as relocated on the same mountain, and the register places it atop Jack Mountain east of Monterey.
The tower came off the original site in 2002 and was reinstalled on Jack Mountain in 2017, so the relocation event dates to 2017.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register says 1935 and Jones and VACo say 1934. The May 1934 Highland Recorder items describe the camp, road and planned tower, and a March 15, 1935 item describes the tower as standing. Work starting in 1934 and the tower standing by March 1935 fits all the sources. The story reports both years.
The register, VACo and Jones date the removal to 2002. A July 24, 2004 Recorder item reports the dismantling. The story uses 2002 for removal and mentions the 2004 item.

notes_for_editor: Original site: FFLA says Tower Gone. Jones describes a CCC camp foundation a short way up the road, not tower footings; no source describes tower remains at the old site. The current tower and its access are covered by us-va-sounding-knob-moved. Access changed over time: fenced in 2017 per Jones, gated but open daylight since November 2020 per the register. Build year 1934 vs 1935 is unresolved in the sources; the story reports both. No new photos added.
